<description>
This adds regression tests for the 64-bit file positions introduced by [bitcoin/bitcoin#36669](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36669). Existing flatfile tests use small offsets. The VARINT overflow tests added in [bitcoin/bitcoin#36725](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36725) don't check that `FlatFilePos` preserves a 64-bit position or that opening a file uses the full offset.

The tests check serialization around 2 GiB and 4 GiB, plus zero and `UINT64_MAX`. They also check opening and seeking around 2 GiB and 4 GiB, including preservation of the position across `size()`. The file stays one byte so no data is written at a large offset.

Validation process:

- On macOS arm64 (Apple Clang 21), Linux x86_64/i386 (GCC 13), and Windows x86_64 (clang-cl 22), `flatfile_tests`, `serialize_tests`, `streams_tests`, and `blockmanager_tests` pass. Include/test linters, changed-range clang-format, and whitespace checks also pass locally.
- Before #36669, the existing flatfile tests pass, while the new tests catch rejected serialization and a seek position wrapping to zero at 4 GiB.
- Casting only the current `FlatFileSeq::Open` seek offset to `uint32_t` also makes the new positioning test fail while existing flatfile tests pass on macOS, Linux x86_64, and Windows x86_64.

On non-Windows systems with 32-bit `long`, the seek test warns and returns because the current wrapper uses `fseek`. The serialization test still runs. This behavior was verified on Linux i386. These were focused checks; the full CI matrix has not run.

CI results: [Linux x86_64](https://github.com/john-lawniczak/bitcoin/actions/runs/43471513629/job/132044496559), [Windows x86_64](https://github.com/john-lawniczak/bitcoin/actions/runs/43471513629/job/132044497097), [Linux i386](https://github.com/john-lawniczak/bitcoin/actions/runs/43472008804/job/132046036624). All jobs tested commit `1d11bd83d892d5bdac759e98321899d60f7c84e8`.
</description>

<commits>
1d11bd83d8 test: Cover 64-bit flatfile position boundaries

Check FlatFilePos serialization against independently encoded 64-bit
positions at the signed and unsigned 32-bit boundaries and UINT64_MAX.

Exercise FlatFileSeq::Open and AutoFile positioning around 2 GiB and
4 GiB, including position preservation across size(). Keep the file at
one byte by never writing past EOF.

Skip large seeks on non-Windows builds with 32-bit long, where the
current FileSeek64 wrapper still uses fseek. Serialization coverage
remains enabled.

Follow-up coverage for bitcoin/bitcoin#36669.
</commits>
